content.text:
I searched the knowledge store once, using four queries, and built this list from those results. I did not run follow-up searches to check for gaps.

I included:
- Fractures of the wrist region, including closed and open wrist fractures.
- Distal radius fractures, including Colles', Smith's, torus and greenstick fractures and radial styloid fractures.
- Distal ulna fractures.
- Carpal bone fractures: scaphoid, lunate, triquetral, pisiform, trapezium, trapezoid, capitate and hamate.
- Wrist fracture-dislocations and fracture-subluxations.

I left out the following:
- Procedures, X-rays and casts.
- Hand, finger and metacarpal fractures.
- Fractures of the radius shaft or proximal radius.
- Generic "fracture of radius" codes.
- Sprains and other non-fracture wrist injuries.
- Sequelae and "history of" codes.

I included two broader codes, S242 and Syu65 ("Fracture at wrist and/or hand level"). They cover the wrist but are not specific to it, so you may want to drop them.

I searched the knowledge store once, using four queries, and built this list from those results. I did not run follow-up searches to check for gaps.

I included:
- Fractures of the wrist region, including closed and open wrist fractures.
- Distal radius fractures, including Colles', Smith's, torus and greenstick fractures and radial styloid fractures.
- Distal ulna fractures.
- Carpal bone fractures: scaphoid, lunate, triquetral, pisiform, trapezium, trapezoid, capitate and hamate.
- Wrist fracture-dislocations and fracture-subluxations.

I left out the following:
- Procedures, X-rays and casts.
- Hand, finger and metacarpal fractures.
- Fractures of the radius shaft or proximal radius.
- Generic "fracture of radius" codes.
- Sprains and other non-fracture wrist injuries.
- Sequelae and "history of" codes.

I searched the knowledge store once, using four queries, and built this list from those results. I did not run follow-up searches to check for gaps.

I included:
- Fractures of the wrist region, including closed and open wrist fractures.
- Distal radius fractures, including Colles', Smith's, torus and greenstick fractures and radial styloid fractures.
- Distal ulna fractures.
- Carpal bone fractures: scaphoid, lunate, triquetral, pisiform, trapezium, trapezoid, capitate and hamate.
- Wrist fracture-dislocations and fracture-subluxations.

- Procedures, X-rays and casts.
- Hand, finger and metacarpal fractures.
- Fractures of the radius shaft or proximal radius.

content.text:
I ran one combined search and built the codelist from its results. I didn't run follow-up searches to check for gaps.

**What I included**
- Wrist-level fracture codes: closed, open and "wrist region" fractures, including the right and left versions.
- Fractures of the lower (distal) end of the radius and ulna. This covers Colles', Smith's, Barton's, Chauffeur's, radial styloid, greenstick and torus-type fractures, with their open and closed forms.
- Carpal bone fractures: scaphoid/navicular, lunate, triquetral, pisiform, trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate, and multiple carpal bones.
- Fracture-dislocations and fracture-subluxations of the wrist.

**What I left out**
- Procedures, X-rays and imaging.
- Sprains, general wrist symptoms and sequelae codes.
- Fractures of the shaft or proximal radius and ulna.
- Metacarpal, hand and finger fractures.
- Galeazzi's fracture, which is a radial shaft fracture.
- Pathological fractures other than the distal radius and ulna ones listed below.

**Judgement calls**
- I included the two "fracture at wrist and/or hand level" codes (S242 and Syu65). They are broader than the wrist, so you may want to drop them.
- I included the Dupuytren's fracture, Hutchinson's fracture and De Quervain's fracture codes as distal radius or radial styloid fractures. This is from their names, not from checking their definitions.
- I included the pathological fracture codes for the distal radius and for the distal radius and ulna together. I left out the distal ulna one.

I ran one combined search and built the codelist from its results. I didn't run follow-up searches to check for gaps.

**What I included**
- Wrist-level fracture codes: closed, open and "wrist region" fractures, including the right and left versions.
- Fractures of the lower (distal) end of the radius and ulna. This covers Colles', Smith's, Barton's, Chauffeur's, radial styloid, greenstick and torus-type fractures, with their open and closed forms.
- Carpal bone fractures: scaphoid/navicular, lunate, triquetral, pisiform, trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate, and multiple carpal bones.
- Fracture-dislocations and fracture-subluxations of the wrist.

**What I left out**
- Procedures, X-rays and imaging.
- Sprains, general wrist symptoms and sequelae codes.
- Fractures of the shaft or proximal radius and ulna.
- Metacarpal, hand and finger fractures.
- Galeazzi's fracture, which is a radial shaft fracture.
- Pathological fractures other than the distal radius and ulna ones listed below.

**Judgement calls**
- I included the two "fracture at wrist and/or hand level" codes (S242 and Syu65). They are broader than the wrist, so you may want to drop them.
- I included the Dupuytren's fracture, Hutchinson's fracture and De Quervain's fracture codes as distal radius or radial styloid fractures. This is from their names, not from checking their definitions.
- I included the pathological fracture codes for the distal radius and for the distal radius and ulna together. I left out the distal ulna one.

I ran one combined search and built the codelist from its results. I didn't run follow-up searches to check for gaps.

**What I included**
- Wrist-level fracture codes: closed, open and "wrist region" fractures, including the right and left versions.
- Fractures of the lower (distal) end of the radius and ulna. This covers Colles', Smith's, Barton's, Chauffeur's, radial styloid, greenstick and torus-type fractures, with their open and closed forms.
- Carpal bone fractures: scaphoid/navicular, lunate, triquetral, pisiform, trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate, and multiple carpal bones.
- Fracture-dislocations and fracture-subluxations of the wrist.

**What I left out**
- Procedures, X-rays and imaging.
- Sprains, general wrist symptoms and sequelae codes.
- Fractures of the shaft or proximal radius and ulna.
- Metacarpal, hand and finger fractures.
- Galeazzi's fracture, which is a radial shaft fracture.
- Pathological fractures other than the distal radius and ulna ones listed below.

**Judgement calls**
- I included the two "fracture at wrist and/or hand level" codes (S242 and Syu65). They are broader than the wrist, so you may want to drop them.
- I included the Dupuytren's fracture, Hutchinson's fracture and De Quervain's fracture codes as distal radius or radial styloid fractures. This is from their names, not from checking their definitions.
- I included the pathological fracture codes for the distal radius and for the distal radius and ulna together. I left out the distal ulna one.
